references.text: The Psalms' description of manna as 'bread from angels' and bread from heaven provides the historical and prophetic context for Jesus' self-understanding as the true bread that gives eternal life.
Here, manna is referred to as bread from heaven, which establishes the typology that Jesus fulfills when he calls himself the bread that came down from heaven.
Jesus' claim to have come down from heaven is a direct reference to his heavenly origin, which is also emphasized in this text about the Son of Man who is in heaven.
Jesus' prayer to give eternal life to those the Father has given him corresponds with the promise in John 6:51 that whoever eats of the bread will live forever.
Jesus' self-identification as the resurrection and the life forms the theological basis for the claim that the bread he gives is his flesh, which gives life to the world.
